text: PRE-REGISTERED RESULT (plan b6b903d9ec37). PRODIGY IC-NIS scored on 15 peptide-AChE complexes (3 candidates x 5 seeds). Discrimination ratio = 1.359: the between-candidate SD (1.4098 kcal/mol) is barely above the within-candidate seed noise (1.0377 kcal/mol). H1 CONFIRMED — PRODIGY does not distinguish different peptides better than reseeding the same one. H2 CONFIRMED — the whole between-candidate range is 2.4434 kcal/mol, 17.1% of the 14.3 kcal/mol range the regression was fitted on.

H3 FALSIFIED, and this refutes the MECHANISM I proposed, not the conclusion. I predicted the %NIS terms would dominate because they are computed over the whole complex and a small peptide barely perturbs a 583-residue receptor's surface. %NIS is indeed nearly constant (41.2-43.2% apolar across all 15 structures), but it accounts for only 10.6% of the between-candidate variance, not the >80% predicted. The variation is driven by the interface-contact terms: BasalSuper-AChE-TrkA-B5 averages 21.0 charged/apolar contacts against AstroEaat2-Up-A2's 10.8. PRODIGY IS responding to the interfaces.

THE OPERATIVE CONCLUSION, and it is the confound I pre-registered rather than a clean verdict on PRODIGY. PRODIGY responds to the interface contacts, but those interfaces are themselves seed-unstable: study #2 measured the across-seed SD of minimum interface PAE at 3.14 Angstrom on these same complexes, and the contact counts swing from 13 to 52 across seeds for one candidate. So the signal PRODIGY extracts is real but is swamped by the instability of what it is reading. This study therefore CANNOT separate 'PRODIGY cannot discriminate here' from 'these interfaces are not real' — exactly the confound stated in the registered plan before any structure was scored. PRODIGY must not be wired into the platform on this evidence.

RETRIEVAL RESOLVED THE SIGN-FLIP MYSTERY. Two earlier memory-based retrievals of the PRODIGY regression produced mutually sign-flipped forms, and both were faithful to a different real source: the published eLife Equation 2 is the EXACT NEGATION of the reference implementation, because the paper regresses against |dG| while the code returns signed dG. Two further published-source corruptions were found: eLife Table 3 Model 6 lists different weights in the 4th decimal (a different fit run), and the official method page misprints the %NIS_charged coefficient as 0.3810 instead of 0.13810. The installed prodigy-prot source was read and matches the retrieved coefficients exactly. This is the clearest demonstration yet of why retrieval beats recall: three published sources disagree, and only reading the code resolves it.

APPLICABILITY, established by retrieval: the string 'peptid' occurs ZERO times in the eLife full text. PRODIGY was fitted on 81 crystal structures of globular protein-protein complexes with interface BSA 808-3370 A^2 and dG from -4.3 to -18.6 kcal/mol. The authors publish no applicability statement covering peptides. Applying it to 26-47mers is an out-of-domain extrapolation with no published validation, and must never be reported as a calibrated dG.

CORRECTION to a premise this project held. PoseBusters' PAPER states it uses RDKit GetBestRMS, but the CODE has never used it for the pass/fail decision at any commit: rmsd.py gates on CalcRMS and reports GetBestRMS only as an auxiliary column. Verified live: for a pose rigidly translated 3.0 A, CalcRMS = 3.0 (fails) while GetBestRMS = 0.0 (would pass). Two errors exist and push in OPPOSITE directions — omitting symmetry correction inflates RMSD (1.5375 A of pure artefact measured on p-nitrophenol), while GetBestRMS deflates it by re-superimposing and hides real placement error. AlignMol commits both at once. Only CalcRMS is correct for docking.
